properties.plan_source: Ballu 1909: 94-95 (BCTH; offprint pp. 22-23, the report on the 1908 excavations) and 1911a (Sept années): 67-68, the room as he describes it; no plan of the house, nothing on the ground; round-2 drawing (Oct 6, 2026)
properties.description: north wall of the concrete room, between it and the third row's west room; Ballu makes the concrete room as deep as the tablinum and at its level (*à la hauteur du tablinum, et de même profondeur que celui-ci*, at the level of the tablinum and of the same depth, 1911a: 68), with the third row's west room north of it, so this wall carries on the line of the hall's north wall; the floor reads flat and grey right across here, and Courtois draws a wall about 0.9 m further north with a short piece hanging down from it, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan, which draws the piece; Ballu 1909: 94-95 (BCTH; offprint pp. 22-23, the report on the 1908 excavations) and 1911a (Sept années): 67-68; round-2 drawing (Oct 6, 2026)
properties.description: partition between the limestone-paved room and the north-east corner room; Ballu's limestone-paved room on the north street and the larger north-east corner room with mosaic traces (1911a: 67); I can't see anything of the partition on the ground, so it's on Courtois's line and uncertain

properties.plan_source: Ballu 1909: 94-95 (BCTH; offprint pp. 22-23, the report on the 1908 excavations) and 1911a (Sept années): 67-68, the room as he describes it; no plan of the house, nothing on the ground; round-2 drawing (Oct 6, 2026)
properties.description: wall between the two tiny rooms on the east street; Ballu says the two tiny rooms together are as deep as the concrete room (*la profondeur de celle-ci était égale à la somme des deux autres*, its depth was equal to the sum of the other two, 1911a: 68) but gives no sizes, and nothing of this wall shows on the ground, so it divides the pair the way Courtois does, a little over half way up from the south wall to the wall above the tiny rooms, uncertain; Courtois's own wall, about a metre thick, is about 0.2 to 1.2 m further north, but his wall above the tiny rooms is about 1.6 m further north than the ground's, and on his line the north tiny room would be under a metre deep inside

properties.plan_source: Courtois 1951 city plan and Wilson 2001's location plan of Timgad (fig. 12.08, p. 279) for the walls of the block; Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32) for the rooms; walls where the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: wall A, between the west and second rooms of the second, third and north rows, between the west room of the north row and the second room of the north row, south of the door; I can barely see anything of it on the ground along this piece, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: not on Courtois 1951 or Wilson 2001, and not in Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32); drawn from the satellite imagery; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: wall between the third and fourth rooms of the second row (ground only), between the third room of the second row and the fourth room of the second row, north of the door; the upper half barely shows at all, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: not on Courtois 1951 or Wilson 2001, and not in Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32); drawn from the satellite imagery; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: wall between the third and fourth rooms of the third row (ground only), between the third room of the third row and the fourth room of the third row, north of the door; north of the door the line fades and I can barely see it, so uncertain

properties.plan_source: not on Courtois 1951 or Wilson 2001, and not in Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32); drawn from the satellite imagery; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: cross wall through the east room of the third row (ground only), between the east room of the third row, south part and the east room of the third row, north part; a faint line across the east room of the third row about 3 m above the second east-west wall, running from the east strip's wall, which has a black pit against its far side, to a black pit against the east wall, bright slabs beside both, on neither plan; between the two pits the ground shows little more than mottled grey, so it's uncertain, and it may be an edge of paving or a bench between two basins rather than a wall; nothing I can really read on the imagery along this piece, so uncertain
